dek: Hidden Falls is the Grand Teton National Park waterfall we cover, on Cascade Creek. Snow often stays in the mountains until mid-July, so check trail conditions first.
overview: Grand Teton National Park is the Teton Range rising over Jackson Hole, with wildlife and lakes below.

Hidden Falls is the waterfall we cover here. USGS places it in the park, on Cascade Creek, and visitors have reviewed it. We don't have a published hike length, elevation or difficulty for it, so check routes and conditions with the park.
fallsIntro: Hidden Falls is the only waterfall we list in the park, and it has no trail details yet, so confirm distances and conditions with the park.
plan: There is no mileage on file, so plan around the snow line. The weather page says snow often remains in the mountains until mid-July, while Moose, at the visitor center, reaches the 80s in summer. Hidden Falls is on Cascade Creek, a mountain creek, so the mountain conditions are the ones that apply.
flow: The Snake River gauge at Moose (USGS 13013650) is about 8 miles from Hidden Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in June at about 6,792 cubic feet per second and was lowest in December at about 775.

Cascade Creek is a small tributary and the Snake measures the valley river, so use this as a rough picture of the melt season rather than a reading for Hidden Falls. Snow on mountain trails can last until mid-July even if the river peaks earlier.
feesLead: There is an entrance fee, no vehicle reservation is needed, and visitors who aren't US residents pay an extra $100 per person. Lodging and campgrounds are separate and can fill months ahead.
access: The fee page says to expect lines at the gates and crowds at popular areas in summer, and that you don't need a reservation to enter. We don't have a shuttle timetable for Hidden Falls on file. Our directory files it under Moose Wilson Road, about 17 miles away in a straight line; that is a place label, not the trailhead name.
safety: The weather page lists afternoon storms, lightning and rockfall as mountain conditions, and says snow can be on trails in summer. We have no waterfall-specific swimming or current warning on file.
